title: Croatia Walks a Tightrope Between Resilience and Reform as Inflation Lingers · 03 Sep
keywords: Croatia, inflation, GDP growth, European Commission, euro area, fiscal policy, cost of living, HICP, Croatian National Bank, OECD, public debt, deficit, economic reform, EU funds
notes: Croatia's economy continues to grow, but slowing momentum and persistent price pressures are testing the government's claim that households are being protected. With inflation projected at 4.6 percent for 2026 and GDP growth forecast to ease to 2.7 percent, Zagreb faces a delicate balancing act between fiscal discipline and public discontent. The country is emerging as a telling case study for the European Union of whether smaller euro-area economies on the periphery can manage growth, disinflation, and budget stability simultaneously.
